## Root cause confirmed, fix merged as Gerrit 3030 (`0ca99c39f90`)

### AC1 — reproduction

The bug is environmental-conditional, and that nearly hid it. An unmodified `origin/main`
PASSES on this host, because Homebrew supplies `/opt/homebrew/bin/flock`. Re-running with
the Homebrew path removed reproduced the CI failure exactly:

```
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"
-> 4 failures, all `flock: command not found`, stale "timed out waiting" diagnostics,
   downstream `git rev-parse HEAD` exit 128
```

That is why a casual local check would have reported "cannot reproduce".

### Correction to the original triage

The filed description implied the `flock(1)` call was newly introduced. It was not. The
green-to-red window is `e50e733aaa3` ("Refresh MCP code workspace on startup"), which added
`tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` and thereby began *exercising* the pre-existing
`with_dir_lock` path on macOS. The latent portability defect predates that commit; the
tests only revealed it.

### Mechanism

`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` depended on util-linux `flock(1)`, which is not present
on macOS. Fixed by using Python stdlib `fcntl.flock` on inherited fd 9.

macOS `fcntl` semantics were verified experimentally rather than assumed:

```
child-exit-parent-fd-open   probe_rc=1 blocked
after-parent-fd-close       probe_rc=0 acquired
crash-release               held_rc=1 blocked; after_kill_rc=0 acquired
```

This proves the child-acquired lock survives the Python helper's exit while the parent
shell holds fd 9, releases when that fd closes, excludes a second holder, and releases
after a holder is killed (AC3, AC5).

### AC7 — the second, masked defect

`with_dir_lock` collapsed `flock` exit 127 (binary absent) and exit 1 (genuine timeout)
into one message: `mcp: timed out waiting for the ... lock`. The real cause was therefore
reported as contention. Now distinguished: `could not acquire ... within N seconds` versus
`lock mechanism unavailable ...`.

### AC8 — red/green on the four CI-red tests

```
# before, no flock(1) on PATH
FAILED test_clean_code_workspace_behind_origin_main_fast_forwards
FAILED test_refresh_emits_workspace_sha_and_distance_from_target
FAILED test_missing_workspace_is_recloned
FAILED test_workspace_with_unresolvable_head_is_recloned
4 failed in 3.43s

# after, same no-flock PATH
4 passed in 2.93s
```

Targeted suites: `test_mcp_entrypoint.py` 15 passed, `test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py`
21 passed, combined 36 passed.

### AC9 — Linux unchanged

Satisfied by `Verified +1` on Gerrit 3030, which is the Linux CI cell.

### AC10 — no new dependency

Shell plus Python stdlib only. No dependency manifest change, no CI-provider-specific path,
so `project.portability` is preserved.

### AC11 — `make verify`

Exactly the 17 known macOS-arm64 pandoc `Bad CPU type` failures, no MCP failures.
Complexity and mechanism ratchets both pass (`active=682 new=26 increased=0 stale=0`; all
reported new entries pre-admitted). A `# mechanism-ok: lock with_dir_lock — 5967-...`
marker was added at the definition site, since this is deliberately a lock-mechanism change.

### AC12 — pending
